regime_context: The detector shows a narrowing eligible universe (19/49) led by AI Infrastructure (score 1.98) with Cybersecurity (score 1.638) the challenger; gate_helps is true so trend-gate discipline has historically cut drawdown on US, but rank-IC is ~0 and rotation timing has no validated edge. Track record (89 calls, dir_accuracy 0.483) suggests past directional calls were near coin-flip — I should default to low conviction and few theses.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Cybersecurity's crowding_z (1.8) rolls over while its durability_bar stays above 0.85 and breadth stays at 1.0 — if crowding_z falls back toward 0.8 or below over the next 10 sessions without losing the trend tag, that would retire the watch and suggest the cybersecurity leg is converting from hot-money to durable leadership.

theses.subject: AI Infrastructure
theses.thesis: This is the incumbent leader and the only eligible theme above durability_bar 0.68 with a non-trending (mixed) Hurst tag — meaning the strength is broad-based leadership rather than an extended trend rip — and it is NOT crowded (z 0.59). Per the guardrails, I should not buy it because it leads; I lean overweight only on the narrow ground that it is the highest-scoring eligible theme with adequate durability and no crowding flag, with the trend gate as the risk discipline. This is a staying-power judgment, not a return forecast.
evidence: gate_helps true — trend discipline is the one validated leg
theses.dissent: The momentum rank itself has no forecast edge, and the mixed Hurst tag plus val_state 'fading' suggests leadership may already be rotating; the high unscheduled-news share (0.75) makes a 20-day hold vulnerable to a headline-driven air pocket.

falsifier.text: SMH lags SPY by 5% or more over a rolling 20-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: This is the confirmed challenger in the rotation read — eligible, scorable, with the strongest trend health (durability_bar 0.85, Hurst 'trend', breadth 1.0). The crowding flag (z 1.8) is a size-down caution only, never a fade. The coherent, broad, trend-consistent profile is the closest thing this state has to a durable non-AI leadership leg.
evidence: crowding_z 1.8 (crowded true) — sizing caution, not a fade signal
theses.dissent: Crowding_z at 1.8 is the highest in the eligible set; per the guardrails, attention spikes and crowding can mark tops, so this is precisely where disciplined size-down (not conviction-up) applies. The high breadth could simply reflect a broad market 'everything software' beta, not theme-specific alpha.

falsifier.text: CIBR fails to outperform XLI by at least 2% over the next 20 trading days while staying above its trend gate

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: The only genuinely trend-consistent non-tech eligible theme: durability_bar 0.68, Hurst 'trend', breadth 0.727, and not crowded (z 0.83). It offers a diversifying leg against the AI/tech concentration without the crowding or mixed-trend caveats of the leaders. This is a conventional trend-following lean under a validated drawdown-control gate.
theses.dissent: Energy complex leadership is coincident and mean-reverting on intermediate horizons historically; the macro backdrop shows no dominant energy narrative in recent flow, and a 0.75 unscheduled-surprise share means commodity-linked themes can gap on news unexpectedly.

falsifier.text: XLE breaks below its own 20-day trend gate before the check-by date or lags SPY by 4% over the window

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
